content.text:
**Context:** Adding WR receiving counts (catches, yards, YAC) from the PFF passing feed to the WR game model, reliability check, and Baylor profiles, then updating Drive files.

**Key Exchanges:**
- Pulled receiving counts for all 9 seasons (2018–2026), 3,588 games, 0 failures (~5 min). Target totals match old files in every season and in all 42,856 WR games.
- WR model test R² rose from 0.14 to 0.46, largely because the PFF grade itself rewards catches and yards, so it is not a new explanation of good grades.
- Baylor WRs vs baseline: +0.17 (range −0.43 to +0.83). The range includes zero, so not a finding.
- Reliability: catches/snap passes fully. Yards/snap and YAC/snap pass with shrinkage. Catch rate, yards/target and YAC/catch fail.
- Catch rates were steady across seasons (62–65%).

**Decisions Made:**
- Built the "decide whether to build" item 3 (WR catches and yards) instead of only deciding. The 3 metrics that passed reliability went into the profiles automatically, adding 3 columns for 5 Baylor WRs. Nothing else in the table changed. User can ask for removal.
- Added the receiving pull to the checkpoint rebuild script so it refreshes on 2026-12-02 (adds ~3 min per restart).
- Recommended option A: keep both catches/snap and the yards metrics, though catches/snap closely tracks targets/snap. Option B is to drop catches/snap.

**Lessons Learned:**
